title: Hello, Python!
body:
Goal: make Python say four things in the Shell.

  1. Open starter.py in Thonny (File > Open...).
  2. Press the green Run button (or F5). Look at the Shell at the bottom: Python says Hello, Python!.
  3. Follow the # TODO comments. Add three more print(...) lines:
    • who is coding today (a nickname is fine - never your full name),
    • your favorite game or animal,
    • a goodbye message that uses the word bye.
  4. Press Run again after every new line.

Remember: Python is picky. print is all small letters, the words go inside "quotes", and every ( needs a ).

Done looks like: four different lines in the Shell, the last one says bye.

Extra: add a comment line (starting with #) that explains your program, or print a tiny picture made of letters, like print("(^_^)").

hints.label: Hint 1
hints.title: Where to look
hints.html: Find the three # TODO comments in starter.py. Each one tells you what to print. Look at the line print("Hello, Python!") that already works, because your new lines will look a lot like it.

hints.label: Hint 2
hints.title: Try this
hints.html: The print command shows words in the Shell. The words go inside quotes, and the quotes go inside the parentheses. Write one new print line under each # TODO, and press Run after each one.

hints.label: Hint 3
hints.title: Almost there
hints.html: Each new line has this shape: print("____"). Put your own words in the blank. Check that every ( has a ) and every opening quote has a closing quote. Your last message needs the word bye somewhere in it.

starter.name: starter.py
starter.raw:
# Hello, Python!
# Lines that start with # are COMMENTS. Python skips them.
# Comments are notes for the people who read your code.

print("Hello, Python!")

# TODO: print who is coding today (a nickname is fine)

# TODO: print your favorite game or animal

# TODO: print a goodbye message that uses the word bye
